brief.headline: Move from 100% advance to 30-day credit — frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash — and close the ₹12.95 L/year price gap to our cheapest supplier.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match the ₹66.48/KG we pay Sayaji Industries for the same Dextrose.
priceAsk.basis: We already buy Dextrose Anhydrous IP at ₹66.48/KG from Sayaji — proven, qualified supplier — and the open market asking price sits in a ₹60–81/kg band (typical ₹66–73/kg), so ₹66.48/KG is market-fair. Sukhjit's ₹70.80/KG is 6.5% above that, costing us an extra ₹12.95 L every year.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Switch from 100% advance payment to standard 30-day credit after delivery.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash that's currently locked in advance payments.

brief.financialLeverage: Sukhjit is big — ₹1555.82 Cr in sales — and growing fast at 29.7% a year, so they want new orders to keep that momentum. But they keep only 2.9% as profit (about ₹3 out of every ₹100 they sell), which means there's not much room for a big price cut without hurting them. We're tiny to them — our ₹1.06 Cr is just 0.07% of their revenue — so we have almost no pull on our own. Their overall health score is D (44/100), meaning they're not in great shape but not in immediate trouble either. The play here: lead with payment terms (easiest win, zero profit impact for them), then use the threat of moving volume to Sayaji or qualifying Gulshan/Sanstar to justify closing the price gap. Don't push so hard on price that you squeeze a low-margin supplier into trouble — win on cash first, price second.

evidence.point: We pay ₹70.80/KG; our cheapest supplier (Sayaji) charges ₹66.48/KG — a 6.5% gap.
That gap costs us ₹12.95 L every year in extra spend.
We pay them 100% in advance; moving to 30-day credit frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash.
They keep only 2.9% as profit, so a deep price cut could destabilize them.
Our ₹1.06 Cr spend is just 0.07% of their ₹1555.82 Cr revenue — we're a very small customer.
They're growing sales at 29.7% a year, so they're hungry for volume commitments.

alternates.name: Sayaji Industries Limited (already qualified)
alternates.why: Currently our cheapest source at ₹66.48/KG for the same Dextrose Anhydrous IP — proven, audited, in our supply base.

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker, ₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health score B (62/100) — a strong drop-in alternate for dextrose; qualify before RFQ.

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist, ₹821.13 Cr revenue, health C (53/100) — growing capacity in starch & dextrose; a lead to qualify.

risks: We're only 0.07% of their business — too small to command much attention on our own; bundle this negotiation with a volume commitment or a longer contract to gain leverage.
Their 2.9% profit margin is razor-thin — pushing too hard on price could force them to cut corners on quality or delivery, or walk away entirely; payment terms are a safer, bigger win.
We're paying 100% in advance right now, which gives them zero reason to negotiate — they have our cash before they ship; flip this to 30-day credit first, then tackle price.

Their health score is D (44/100) and their debt is 0.55x equity — not distressed, but not rock-solid either; if you push too hard and they stumble, you'll need Gulshan or Sanstar qualified and ready to step in.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to standard 30-day payment terms and bring your price in line with the ₹66.48/KG we already pay Sayaji for the same Dextrose — here's how we can make that work for both of us.
